reference_change.title: PERF: speed up array_equal for equal_nan=True

workload.command: python -I -c "import timeit, numpy as np; a = np.random.default_rng(0).standard_normal(1_000_000); a[::7] = np.nan; b = a.copy(); print(min(timeit.repeat(lambda: np.array_equal(a, b, equal_nan=True), number=20, repeat=5)))"
workload.source: written here from the description of https://github.com/numpy/numpy/pull/30810 (array_equal with equal_nan=True): two equal one-million-element float arrays with every seventh value NaN

oracle.source: the array_equal tests in numpy's test_numeric module, run against the installed package (numpy refuses to import from its source tree); targeted tests only

evidence.note: description, as matched by the miner: speedup claims: 4.5× faster; 2.2× faster | timings: 1ms; 0.08ms; 0.2μs; 0.4μs

status_reason: built here and ran workload and oracle on the task and reference trees; see runs. Built from source with the tree's build requirements; the install is not editable, so the tests run against the built package
